title: Re-Volt/Tracks
text:
There are fifteen tracks which you can choose to play. Initially, only easy tracks will be available for you to choose to race at, and you can only unlock other tracks when you finish all championships either first or second or third, or beat all time trials. You can choose how many laps you want to race for. Minimum amount of laps for each track is one while maximum amount of laps for each track is twenty. There are four variants for each track: Normal, Mirrored, Reverse, and Reverse-Mirrored.

Toys in the Hood 1
thumb|Toys in the Hood 1 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 1 screenshot
 Name: Toys in the Hood 1
 Length: 747 meters (737 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Easy
 Challenge Time: 00:54:000

Toys in the Hood 1 is first track in the game and first track of Easy difficulty set in suburbia that starts at construction site and takes you around residential buildings where racing line and track layout are very open and wide. All racers start on edge of construction site. Ahead is T-intersection at which racers will have to turn right. Smooth left bend follows that leads to acute right turn. Long straight ensues, before leading to another T-intersection where cars must turn left. Afterwards, right turn leads to another long straight before another right turn. What follows is curvy bend where racers have an option to cut corners using curbs. Following another right turn will lead into loop, arriving back at second T-intersection where competitors drive back to starting line in reverse, but instead must enter construction pipe that lies on left side on first T-intersection. Construction pipe is dark and narrow compared to rest of track. Pipe eventually leads to construction site where racers must climb steep ravine back onto road that leads back to starting line. Normal variant of Toys in the Hood 1 is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time. Mirrored variant of Toys in the Hood 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Easy tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Toys in the Hood 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Easy tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Toys in the Hood 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Easy tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

There is basketball at end of main straightway that bounces out into road on first lap. While not as heavy as Ball Bearing Power-Up, it can still spin car out and cause it to lose speed. There are also some traffic cones scattered around streets that get in way when making shortcuts on corners. Construction pipe is also narrow, which promotes lot of carnage there. Finally, because various portions of track are shared between both directions, you must be wary of oncoming opponents because bumping into them will cause loss of speed and time for both, and this is exacerbated in Simulation mode. This scenario is especially apparent after starting line in subsequent laps for those leading, and conversely just before construction pipe for those trailing.

Strategies

Sidewalks are great way to cut corners because most of them have inclined entrances, allowing you to drive onto them. However, cars will gain slight amount of air time, which can potentially cause time to be lost in long run if performed frequently. There is also shortcut consisting of narrow route right after first long bend that ends adjacent to red parked car on main straightaway. However, shortcut is ineffective due to wide open nature of track because speed reached in shortcut is much lower than speed reached on normal route. Better take sidewalk cuts. As mentioned before, construction pipe is small and narrow, making trap Pick Ups like Clone Pick Up Power-Up and Oil Slick Power-Up much more effective, so it is advised to place it in this section. Alternatively, placing lone Pick Up Power-Up and Oil Slick Power-Up just before or right after tunnel is good idea.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is above parked red car on main straightway. There is ramp leaning against back of red car; line up and hit it full speed (on Rookie car) to nab it. Higher-rank cars will need to reduce speed near top, or else they will fly clear over Global Pulse Power-Up that is located on top of red car with ramp behind. In Practice Mode, Secret Star is located under parked car on sidewalk near main straightaway.

SuperMarket 2
thumb|SuperMarket 2 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 2 screenshot
 Name: SuperMarket 2
 Length: 301 meters (299 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Easy
 Challenge Time: 00:24:000

SuperMarket 2 is second track in the game and second track of Easy difficulty set in small grocery store where in the middle of track lies storage freezer that is track's most distinctive feature. All racers start at entrance of supermarket. Ahead are three aisles that open up four lanes, giving you choice whichever lane you would like to take. Either way, they all lead to soft right bend, which follows into meat freezer storage. Racers then traverse freezer section which consists of very wide 180 degree turn, then leading to exit of storage. Sharp left bend follows into another hard right in quick succession. Racers than drive straight ahead to checkout registers, which once again provide many lanes from their presence. Exit of grocery store follows soon after, and you will drive on straight-dipped sidewalk that lies just outside market. At end of sidewalk is right turn back into entrance of supermarket. Normal variant of SuperMarket 2 is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time. Mirrored variant of SuperMarket 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Easy tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of SuperMarket 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Easy tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of SuperMarket 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Easy tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Meat storage that is cold freezer where surface of meat locker is very icy and slippery, diminishing cars's traction and causing them to slide when turning. RWD cars in particular are much more dire in this situation because power from rear of their wheels cause them to spin out. Near exit of grocery store are two trolleys right after checkouts. Trolleys's heavy weight will cause any unsuspecting racers to lose almost all of their speed should one come into contact with one. Exit also is supported through automatic sliding doors that move in and out periodically, potentially sliding into paths of unfortunate racers. Near end is entrance of market follows right immediately after peak elevation of sidewalk. You must be cautious in this section or risk spinning out upon landing, which will make or break race because it is final turn of track.

Strategies

FWD and 4WD cars can overcome freezer section thanks to their good grip. While freezer section is trickiest obstacle of track, there are some areas in which surface is completely dry. They lie on the inside and outside perimeters of meat locker. You can cut across to this section in particular inside corner, saving time and navigating through hazard with ease. You can alternatively slow down before undertaking section for extra control. Furthermore, Oil Slick Power-Up or even any havoc in particular are also devious in this section, giving opposing racers no chance of recovery due to friction-less surface. Take rightmost lane in both aisles and checkout registers because these lanes are closest to following corner. After checkout registers, Clone Pick Up Power-Up and Ball Bearing Power-Up are effective in sidewalk because it is quite narrow and follows from blind corner.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is located on left end of sidewalk that follows after sliding doors. In Practice Mode, Secret Star is located in air above middle register. By hitting ramp at fast speed, car should fly right into airborne Secret Star. You will need fast or high accelerating car to get Secret Star that is in air.

Museum 2
thumb|Museum 2 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 3 screenshot
 Name: Museum 2
 Length: 600 meters (600 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Easy
 Challenge Time: 00:45:000

Museum 2 is third track in the game and third track of Easy difficulty set in natural history museum containing many ancient artifacts and planetarium that compromises large portion of course layout and which is it's biggest feature. All racers start at glass walkway with two skeletal dinosaur models. Bridge leads to hallway composed of slight right bend. Hallway takes you to first part of museum that is artifact showcase. Series of narrow small curves ensue, followed into small room consisting of more extinct dinosaur skeletal models. At end of room is sharp right that leads into entrance of planetarium called "Space Race". Entrance of space museum consists of two escalators which are left and right. Left side moves upwards while right side moves downwards. Inclines lead to very wide straightaway with concept artwork of various planets and space prototypes seen on walls. Tight right turn leads to planetarium's main display of planets in Solar System surrounded by circular glass walkway branching off into two directions and converging at top of circuit following into straightaway into large round turn. You can see more factual information of planets and spaceship replica of Lunar Lander in this room. Turn leads to exit of planetarium and into hallway that slopes straight down. At end of slope leads to another incline where few small turns follows after jump, leading to another hallway which features skeletal models of various sea animals. Start line lies right after this hallway. Normal variant of Museum 2 is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time. Mirrored variant of Museum 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Easy tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Museum 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Easy tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Museum 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Easy tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Museum 2's hallways are very narrow, which in turn punishes cars with poor turning radius. Glass surfaces in particular are fairly smooth, which diminishes grip of some cars, especially RWD cars. Replicas can prove to be obstacle because running into those can waste time. Downhill slope can be very difficult passageway due to speed gained during this section. For some cars, steering sharply at this stage can cause them to lose control, so caution is advised. There is also "Wet Floor" signboard that acts as inconvenient ramp after slope, causing unsuspecting racers to go through it and fly off desired racing line. After downhill slope is secret alternative route that is pointless because it doesn't save time, and is intended rather to confuse you.

Strategies

Pick Ups are effective in narrow hallways. Trap Pick Ups like Clone Pick Up Power-Up, Ball Bearing Power-Up, and Oil Slick Power-Up are very effective in these areas. Oil Slick Power-Up also works best in surfaces colored black, such as in planetarium, because it's difficult to spot where Oil Slick Power-Up is dropped. As for racing line strategies, always take escalator which supports your direction. Entering wrong side will cause significant loss in speed and time. There is also small shortcut right before downhill ramp in which you can enter site of lunar lander replica instead of going around it. Viability of this shortcut is questionable due to moon-like terrain at site that causes cars to lose speed upon entrance. Cars emphasis on off-road capabilities can travel through the shortcut much quicker than usual.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is located on stairs in front of large Ammonite shell that follows right after downhill slope. In Practice mode, Secret Star is located on divider of escalators where it's best to approach from top end of divider because incline is less steep there.

Botanical Garden
thumb|Botanical Garden as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 4 screenshot
 Name: Botanical Garden
 Length: 323 meters (333 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Easy
 Challenge Time: 00:29:000

Botanical Garden is fourth track in the game and fourth track of Easy difficulty set in greenhouse with many elements of nature that includes many plants, bushes, particle effects, and sound effects that make it to be rather realistic racing line. All racers start at enrance of greenhouse where 90 degree right turn lies ahead of them, leading into very large incline. Wide right turn follows, taking you to narrow exit of greenhouse into garden outdoors. Exit brings into right elevated bend. After immediate left turn, you will then travel across bridge in garden. Path then branches off into two directions, which converge shortly after. Wide 180 degree turn surrounding garden's fountain then ensues, leading into narrow tunnel. At end of the tunnel is ramp, landing racers on elevated platform. Small straightaway follows after, and cars will encounter very large drop-off that lies just before start of greenhouse. Normal variant of Botanical Garden is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time. Mirrored variant of Botanical Garden is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Easy tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Botanical Garden is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Easy tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Botanical Garden is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Easy tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Most challenging aspects of Botanical Garden are undoubtedly it's large sudden inclines in areas like jump after fountain, steep slope after 90 degree corner, and greenhouse's exit that could prove troublesome for cars with poor grip, acceleration, or stability, because these corners can make them spin out, sluggish, or flip over respectively.

Strategies

Because Botanical Garden track has bumpy and steep terrain, it is advised to use well-rounded car, especially those with good acceleration and stability. There are also two narrow passageways: One after greenhouse and another after fountain. Using trap Pick Ups like Clone Pick Up Power-Up and Oil Slick Power-Up there will increase chances of landing hit, which in particular is very useful after fountain, because opposing racers may not make platform, giving them ahead larger gap. In terms of best racing line, right path from branch is noticeably faster because it lacks upward inclines. There is also shortcut that allows you to cut right through fountain instead of going around it. However, it's difficult to take due to how narrow path is. Cars with good control and high acceleration can take advantage of this shortcut more easily.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is located on left side of steep slope after two lakes. Border of left lake can be used as ramp to nab star much faster. It is easier to take star in Reverse version of Botanical Garden. In Practice mode, Secret Star is located inside a secret area.

Toy World 1
thumb|Toy World 1 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 5 screenshot
 Name: Toy World 1
 Length: 354 meters (406 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Medium
 Challenge Time: 00:27:000

Toy World 1 is fifth track in the game and first track of Medium difficulty set in huge children's playroom where toys like trucks and arcade games can be seen littered throughout entire place. All racers start at short timber-floored straightaway where ahead of them is helicopter marked with letter 'P' that starts hovering upward after race starts. At end of small straight is tight S-bend leading to moderate-elevated green-carpeted incline steering to right. This leads to second timber floor with another brief straightaway. Second straightaway leads to wide blue-carpeted slim-elevated staircase curve. Alternatively, you may bear to right which consists of narrow path that finishes at dead end. From there, cars drop-off back into main path where staircase was, transforming into very long straightaway that compromises interactive electronic keyboard narrow strip that racers must drive on to progress. Wide right curve then ensues, taking racers under green dinosaur toy, placed right under dip of track. Following dip is another slight right bend that gradually increases in elevation, which climaxes onto steep ramp. Racers fly off ramp, taking them back to start line on lowest floor. In Reverse version of Toy World 1, racers travel into room that lies right beneath large ramp that lead into dinosaur toy. There is also dark yellow tunnel located after interactive piano that is accessible only in Reverse version of Toy World 1, which is path that needs to be taken because it's pointless climbing up stair case. Tunnel ends into tight hairpin that takes racers into path that lies right before peak of staircase. Normal variant of Toy World 1 is unlocked when you win Bronze Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of Toy World 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Medium tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Toy World 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Medium tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Toy World 1 unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Medium tracks in Time Trial mode. 

Obstacles

Large portion of Toy World 1 is covered under carpeted barriers which have small but noticeable difference on grip than surfaces such as tarmac in Toys in the Hood 1. Blue stairwells is easily track's biggest obstacle because consecutive and sudden elevation drops are hazard for cars with poor stability, which is exacerbated abecause obstacle is also bend, forcing cars to also turn while running down stairs. Although this isn't present in right path, it is compensated from large drop-off at end, punishing cars with relatively stiff suspension. Legs of dinosaur toy is also obstruction in tracks. Cars who don't align themselves at start of dip which follows right after bend will collide with pillars, wasting precious time. In lower passageway which lies ahead of racers in start line, as well as in entrance of dark yellow tunnel in Reverse version of Toy World 1 are building blocks stacked on track, obstructing racing line. Colliding with blocks will cause responsible car to lose control and collapse stack which will then scatter ABC blocks all over place. Blocks after being scattered are still reasonable obstacle in course.

Strategies

Toy World 1's straightaways are critical section for using firing Pick Ups like Firework Power-Up, Firework Pack Power-Up, and Water Balloon Power-Up, making aiming lot more easier than normal. Place Oil Slick Power-Up and Clone Pick Up Power-Up on narrow path that lies on right side of staircase because it's extremely effective area that forces opposing racers to take more difficult route instead. Another great place for placing Oil Slick Power-Up and Clone Pick Up Power-Up is electronic keyboard beacuse it's very narrow, guaranteeing opposing racers suffering huge punishment because they won't be able to avoid Oil Slick Power-Up and Clone Pick Up Power-Up placed in that area. Ball Bearing Power-Up is most effective at area with dinosaur toy because dip is blind corner, causing unsuspecting racers to run straight into the item, or swerve away from it and risk hitting green pillars.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is located on left of blue-carpeted stairs. In Practice mode, Secret Star is located before soccer field behind final ramp. You must drop off at ramp at slowest speed or risk flying over it. Secret Star can quickly be obtained by heading towards floor below ramp, then taking sharp left after exiting floor.

Ghost Town 1
thumb|Ghost Town 1 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 6 screenshot
 Name: Ghost Town 1
 Length: 324 meters (335 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Medium
 Challenge Time: 00:30:000

Ghost Town 1 is sixth track in the game and second track of Medium difficulty set in abandoned Western town where wooden buildings such as general stores, guns shop, banks, hotels, and saloons can be seen throughout entire place. All racers start in front of town marshal's hall building called "Voltstone" where you must make immediate left turn when race starts and head for narrow alley that leads to heart of town. Afterwards, racers head towards gallows, entering from the left, and must circle around it before coming back. However, instead of returning back into alley, hard left occurs after heading back, leading into town's bank called "Bargly's Bank". Entering into bank will lead to very sharp right turn instantaneously after exit of bank. Alternatively, you can choose to go around the bank, forgoing distance in return for entrance at high speed in track's next section. Cars will then travel in long but narrow straightway under shelter of large building. Straight eventually leads into steep incline. Sharp right follows right immediately after peak of jump. From there, you have option to travel back onto dirt path or continue on balcony. On first route, racers drive from downwards incline which compensates for upward slope just earlier. 90 degree right then follows, leading to long stretch back to starting line. For second route, racers must take the right turn earlier to continue on balcony, which is also heading towards start line. However, there is no downhill slope in this section, forcing vehicles to drop-off when balcony roof ends. Normal variant of Ghost Town 1 is unlocked when you win Bronze Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of Ghost Town 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Medium tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Ghost Town 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Medium tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Ghost Town 1 unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Medium tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Ghost Town 1 features bumpy and off-road terrain spreading entire track. In contrast to previous tracks which is formed with flat terrain with almost no change in surface properties, Ghost Town 1 is considered to be first off-road themed track in game. Vehicles with poor stability may experience difficulty with this track. Many sections of track are also narrow, such as entrance to shelter or alleyway at start of race, emphasizing use of caution. Throughout track are multiple boxes, planks, and barrels that can obstruct racing line of many players, wasting time. One such example are barrels and crates that are positioned underneath gallows. Bank also has chair that also proves to be an obstacle. Regardless of whichever route you take, both options are dramatic elevation change into ground level. Landing onto dirt road may cause some cars to lose control, which can be very detrimental to race because it is positioned right near start line.

Star Locations

As with many narrow sections, trap Pick Ups like Clone Pick Up Power-Up and Oil Slick Power-Up are effective because they can guarantee hits. Placing Clone Pick Up Power-Up and Oil Slick Power-Up at shelter, alleyway, or even balcony are some examples of strategic approaches. Path used to go around the gallows is shared, which allows you to attack opposing racers who already completed noose structure with Pick Ups like Electro Pulse Power-Up and Shockwave Power-Up, allowing you to catch up to them. As for most optimal racing line, you can go right under gallows instead of traveling perimeter around it. However, you will then risk hitting barrels under it. Next, you must drive onto bank because it's small distance outweighs advantage of higher speed of entry for other route, especially with cars who are adept at acceleration. Near end is recommended to continue onto balcony because racing line is fairly clear there. It's also recommended to slow down just before incline after shelter for maximum control. Avoid traveling on sidesteps of the buildings, especially at heart of western town because inclines waste more time than usual.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is located on sidesteps of "Baynes Hotel" where it can be easily seen after making 180 degree turn around gallows. In Practice mode, Secret Star is on top of box besides ramp that lies few meters behind start line. Some degree of luck will require of you to drop off at correct position, speed, and angle in order to land on box and collect Secret Star.

Toy World 2
thumb|Toy World 2 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 7 screenshot
 Name: Toy World 2
 Length: 444 meters (433 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Medium
 Challenge Time: 00:37:000

Toy World 2 is seventh track in the game and third track of Medium difficulty set in huge children's playroom where toys like trucks and arcade games can be seen littered throughout entire place just like in Toy World 1. All racers start at start of narrow long stretch. Intersecting this path is railway crossroad for large trains that appear every now and then. Long straight results in moderate 180 degree right turn, leading to yet another railway crossing. After crossing is slight right turn, but is immediately followed by very sharp left hairpin. Track then branches off into two different paths. First route features wide left tur while second route follows through dark tunnel which eventually leads to small jump across first path. Both routes then converge. Acute left turn follows, leading racers up to incline. After small straight, racers then make hard right 180 degree turn with very sharp drop in elevation. Two soft left bends subsequently follow, culminating in moderate right bend with upward slope featuring fire-breathing dragon. Normal variant of Toy World 2 is unlocked when you win Bronze Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of Toy World 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Medium tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Toy World 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Medium tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Toy World 2 unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Medium tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Toy World 2 is tougher than Toy World 1 because of increased amount of curves and elevations. Vehicles with poor acceleration and turning radius will tend to struggle in this track because they will be very slow around many of it's corners. Most notable feature of Toy World 2 is yellow-carpeted steep turn that lies few seconds away from starting line. Reckless drivers who undertake corner at very fast speed will most likely lose control and flip over. As one of final corners in track, it can make or break race. Toy World 2 also has large toy trains pass by crossings every once in a while, which is track's most significant obstacle. Wheels of trains will obstruct racing line for many racers, and contact with them will cause cars to be disrupted heavily, wasting precious time. Aside from that, Toy World 2 doesn't have many explicit obstacles, it's track's layout itself that forms crux of it's difficulty.

Strategies

Due to narrow and tight turns, vehicles with excellent acceleration and handling characteristics perform best in this tracks. There is very narrow strip that follows right after first railway crossing. Trap Pick Ups like Oil Slick Power-Up and Clone Pick Up Power-Up are very effective there, guaranteeing hits. Due to shortness of track's walls, it's viable technique to send opponents across sidewalks. Pick Ups like Clone Pick Up Power-Up, Shockwave Power-Up, Firework Power-Up, and Fireworks Pack Power-Up can send opposing racers flying outside boundaries of track. At fork intersection, left route is superior because it's easier as route only consists of wide left turn, compared to tight turn and final jump in right route. It's also risky to go at right route because failing jump will cause significant time to be lost because second part after jump is much shorter.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is located at top right corner of crossing jump at second route when paths branch off. Angle your car to Global Pulse Power-Up's location to reach it, or make jump and drive across edge of ramp. In Practice mode, Secret Star is located at bottom left corner of crossing jump at second route when paths branch off where you can collect it by simply driving across edge of ramp.

Toys in the Hood 2
thumb|Toys in the Hood 2 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 8 screenshot
 Name: Toys in the Hood 2
 Length: 592 meters (592 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Hard
 Challenge Time: 00:45:000 (00:48:000 in Reverse)

Toys in the Hood 2 is eighth track in the game and first track of Hard difficulty set in suburbia that starts at construction site and takes you around more complex neighborhood full of realistic houses, gardens and sprinklers as land obstacles, house items such as doors, skateboards, kitchen chairs, and garden river with more routes and bridges. All racers start at street in neighborhood where beginning of race is marked by a pair of briefs labelled with "Start Race". Street follows wide right bend, which gradually decreases in elevation. Long straightaway ensues which also passes by cross-intersection, taking you into interior of house first. In house is sharp left corner that leads into kitchen where vehicles then exit into house's garden which consists of narrow left bend, leading into shed in garden that leads into tarmac alleyway where there is 90 degree right turn at start of this section. Alleyway then results in left hairpin turn, which then takes racers toward another backyard. Entrance to backyard comprises of very small gap in wall. Through garden, racers then head through next alley, taking them through soft left curve which then takes them through yet another backyard. Hard left occurs as soon as cars enter yard where ahead of them lies small passageway into garage of another house. Racers exit garage by making right turn, taking them back onto left side of intersection. Another straight occurs here, leading to another backyard that consists of water-filled trenches. Racers can take wooden bridge and platform that lies on top of these trenches to go over them. Backyard ends in narrow path, taking racers back to starting line with right turn into street. Normal variant of Toys in the Hood 2 is unlocked when you win Silver Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of Toys in the Hood 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Hard tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Toys in the Hood 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Hard tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Toys in the Hood 2 unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Hard tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Unlike Toys in the Hood 1, Toys in the Hood 2 extends it's racing line into houses's backyards, featuring lot of obstacles, like skateboards, trash cans, shed ramps, and sprinklers. Many components of alleys between gardens are formed by very narrow corners which makes it easy for car to collide against walls. All gardens are comprised of grass surfaces, which impacts grip of many cars. Cars with average to poor grip may experience trouble in these sections. Last garden contains small stream and bridge that are considered most difficult point of this Toys in the Hood 2 because it's very bumpy and features sharp increases in elevation that lead into final alleyway. As final section of track, how well cars perform in this section could be difference between losing and winning.

Strategies

Although slightly more difficult, it is possible to take right sidewalk instead of street at first corner. This is only possible in laps other than first lap because entrance to sidewalk is located little before start line. Alleyways are also narrow, making Pick Ups like Clone Pick Up Power-Up and Oil Slick Power-Up quite effective there, but you must place them right before corners for maximum utility. Ball Bearing Power-Up is also useful at blind corners. With plethora of narrow entrances into backyards, it may also be wise to reduce speed before entering section, especially with grass surfaces that are encountered as soon as cars enter garden. By doing this, you can maintain maximum traction and control. Avoid any ramps whenever possible, including small shed after interior of house, and go around it instead. Furthermore, in final backyard, you must drive right under bridge and go across plank whenever possible.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is located on left sidewalk near start line besides parked red car. Entrance of sidewalk is right under car. In Practice mode, Secret Star is located on top of trash can which lies outside garage. You will need to take left at intersection and hit wooden ramp at correct speed and angle to grab Secret Star. It is also advised to move cone away from path, because it will be somewhat of obstruction in your path.

Toytanic 1
thumb|Toytanic 1 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 9 screenshot
 Name: Toytanic 1
 Length: 742 meters (742 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Hard
 Challenge Time: 00:55:000

Toytanic 1 is ninth track in the game and second track of Hard difficulty set in open seas on ship called Toytanic whose name is obviously pun on ship called Titanic that sank in early hours of 15th of April in 1912 as result of striking iceberg on her maiden voyage from Southampton, England, to New York City, United States. All racers start on first deck of ship where ahead of them is very long straightaway, with divider that splits road into two lanes. Right lane which is sheltered and contains Pick Ups, but is littered with outdoor chairs. At end of long road is ship's leisure section that contains pool coupled with beach balls. Racers go around this section, and head to incline taking them to middle deck of ship. On second floor, another long straight ensues, although it's quite narrower than first straightway. Second straightaway contains wooden ramp that tempts racers to jump over lifebuoy arc. At end of straightaway is 90 degree right turn, which leads to another of same turn back to back. Another ramp is seen just few meters ahead, now taking racers to top of ship. Sharp right occurs right after cars make it on top floor. Racers then go around pipes of ship in order to reach front cabin. After exiting cabin, there is long stretch that eventually ends in left turn, taking cars to a small steel-meshed enclosure on second floor where racers will make sharp 180 degree right turn, leading them right back onto bottom deck. Same divided straightaway as seen near start line occurs again, which eventually leads to large jump to front hull of ship. There is sharp right bend at end. Following path takes racers to final jump back to starting line. Normal variant of Toytanic 1 is unlocked when you win Silver Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of Toytanic 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Hard tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Toytanic 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Hard tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Toytanic 1 unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Hard tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Unique feature of Toytanic 1 is it's "ship turbulence" that stimulates rocking effect of ship that is caused by ocean waves. that in gameplay terms increase or decrease car's top speed periodically. In Time Trial mode, this has luck factor because it's desirable to have increased top speed on straightaways. In other modes, you must be cautious if top speed of your car increases right before corner, which could mean disaster if you are careless. Luckily, turbulence is less drastic in Toytanic 1. Although most of track consists of wide straightaways, Toytanic 1 is formed by several 90º narrow corners which pressure various cars to understeer. There are also ramps and elevations which are transitions from one floor to another which are characterized by their distinctive red steel mesh surface. These areas may prove to be problem to cars with poor stability statistics. Toytanic 1's corners, especially ones on top of ship are open-ended, and could cause confusion for some racers. By following directions seen on HUD, this hazard can be prevented. Deck chairs, lifebuoys, and chimneys are part of Toytanic 1's obstacles list. Pool on ship is water hazard that punishing those who recklessly try cutting through bend. Cars who fall into pool won't be able to get back up on track under normal circumstances, forcing you to reposition which is only way out. There are also deck chairs scattered across track that prove to be nuisance at times. Ultimately, while Toytanic 1 is track with many long stretches, apparent simplicity of track is complicated with multiple obstacles and tight narrow corners that can occur abruptly, especially after end of straightaways.

Strategies

It is best to take advantage of Toytanic 1's straights rather than it's corners and ramps. Consider forgoing stability and go for speed when selecting car. Pick Ups in shelters of straightaways can be worthwhile when you are in need of them because deck chairs are easily avoided as obstacles. Wooden ramps should be avoided, in particular ramp that allows cars to cross pool, and ramp for lifebuoy arc. Pool ramp is not optimal because there is large risk of failing the jump, causing responsible car to fall into pool, wasting a lot of time. Most cars will either lose control or will be forced to make sharp right turn after landing if they even manage to make jump due to height of jump and landing point being inconveniently located right before wall. Lifebuoy ramp wastes time because vehicles will almost always hit lifebuoy rather than go through it. Narrow straights, especially on second floor, and ramp that exits steel surfaced enclosure are good positions to use Clone Pick Up Power-Up and Oil Slick Power-Up because small width of those sections guarantees hits. In addition, straightways are also good places to attack with Water Balloon Power-Up, Firework Power-Up, and Firework Pack Power-Up because open road leaves racers vulnerable.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is located on steel-meshed enclosure on far left where it's located at dead end. In Practice mode, Secret Star is located few meters before finish line, floating in middle of path, where you will need car with a high top speed is required in order to use red ramp to pick it up.

Museum 1
thumb|Museum 1 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 10 screenshot
 Name: Museum 1
 Length: 668 meters (662 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Hard
 Challenge Time: 01:01:000 (00:59:000 in Reverse)

Museum 1 is tenth track in the game and third track of Hard difficulty set in natural history museum that heavily features Egyptian exhibits in contrast to space exhibits in Museum 2. Museum 1 is infested with hard-avoiding obstacles and requires extreme use of tight and narrow turns, for which is considered to be one of hardest tracks in game, with it's difficulty comparable to some of tracks in Extreme difficulty. All racers start in foyer of the museum labelled with queue gate. Ahead of racers is ramp that takes them upwards. Sharp 90 degree right turn occurs right at peak of ramp, followed by soft right bend. Tight left hairpin occurs, which leads to steep downwards slope, with imminent left turn at end that leads racers to dinosaur display room. As soon as cars enter room, they must make immediate right turn indicated by sign ahead of them and head towards hallway that starts with strong left turn. Long straightaway then ensues. At middle of straightaway is dark passageway that has upward inclining ramp that takes you to next level of museum which is Egyptian section where straight ends into blind left corner through very short tunnel which eventually leads you right onto display of ancient Egyptian scarab. After display, there are two opening hallways, in which racers must first take right one. Cars can either drop off display to reach entrance or can bear right where there is narrow tunnel that is normally used in Reverse version of Museum 1. Both paths lead into museum's main dinosaur exhibit which consists of Triceratops skeleton above luxurious red carpet. At end of the exhibit is hard narrow left turn that leads to empty room where racers must reach end of room from left side, do 180 degree turn into right side as denoted by oncoming sign where cars must drive on opposite direction, and head back onto fork intersection where they entered hallway, and this time take first path. Following sharp left on first hallway leads into a room with ramp taking them to another level where racers can either take left or right turn. Left path leads to section with multitude of tables in which racers must go over, and narrow S-bend after room with tables, culminating to final left turn onto narrow blue scaffold that lies just above main floor of museum. After small jump from ramp and quick right turn, racers are taken back to starting line. Taking right path leads you onto dark balcony that is located on top of empty room where 180 degree left turn occurs on balcony, taking you to highly secured room that contains many precious artifacts inside that is used only in Reverse version of Museum 1. There is left turn at end of room that will lead back onto main floor.  Normal variant of Museum 1 is unlocked when you win Silver Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of Museum 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Hard tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Museum 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Hard tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Museum 1 unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Hard tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Unlike Museum 2, Museum 1 exaggerates closed narrow corners which makes cars collide constantly, mainly at first descent road (with Egyptian columns at sides) where you must slow down to avoid crashing. Also, some meters after, cars are thrown under corridor wall due jump beside it, which is by far one of Museum 1's hardest obstacles, as there is also a luck factor inherent to this section. Triceratops's feet are obstruction because they act as inconvenient bump on road. Going over it risks major derailment, wasting time. Avoiding this is difficult because raised platform of red carpet partially conceals hazard, giving you very little time to react. Room with two tables in particular also prove to be major hazard because they are located near final stages of track. Take care not to collide with legs of table because they will scatter cars quite badly. Distance between preceding corner and room is very little, giving you almost no time to react. Last jump through narrow and exposed scaffold is also difficult because it requires you to angle your vehicle correctly before entering. Missing final ramp could make or break race. In Reverse version of Museum 1, going right in center of highly secured room's exit will result in you hitting Ammonite shell that is placed close to front of exit, getting you stuck and losing valuable time if your car is too slow to jump over it, which is evident with AI constantly bumping straight into pedestal on which Ammonite shell is placed once it gets stuck there when using cars with poor top speed and acceleration. You can bypass Ammonite shell if you head into exit of highly secured room either from left or right sides, but you will need luck to land on slope because there is chance you will land on stairs that are on left and right sides of slope, losing valuable time in process. Overall, combination of Museum 1's complex and narrow layout and it's near-unavoidable obstacles makes it one of most grueling and brutal tracks in the game, demanding great deal of memorisation from you to succeed. Tasks such as beating Challenge times in Time Trial are much more difficult in Museum 1 as result.

Strategies

Due to countless amount of tight narrow turns in Museum 1, cars with an emphasis on acceleration and handling shine best here because they will have easier time navigating through course than others. Trap Pick Ups like Oil Slick Power-Up and Clone Pick Up Power-Up work best in narrow sections, which are ubiquitous in this track. Some notable examples are corners before and after room with two tables, scaffolding, and hairpin turn in empty room. Whole path on right hallway from fork intersection is shared because racers will eventually have to travel whole path in reverse after main hairpin turn at end of empty room, giving you good opportunity to use Electro Pulse Power-Up to zap any cars that pass by from opposite direction and allowing you to catch up to lead position if you incapacitate any opposing racers that are ahead of you. Avoid using Oil Slick Power-Up and Clone Pick Up Power-Up before hairpin because there is chance you may fall into your own trap travelling back. As for most optimal racing line, you must orient your car before drop-off to enter second hallway directly to save time turning on ground. It's also recommended to take left turn at Ammonite shell display room because balcony turn on right option is excessively time-consuming. 

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is after Egyptian room behind sign board at jump edge. Slow down before grabbing Global Pulse Power-Up in order to prevent falling off display case inadvertently. In Practice mode, Secret Star is floating at great height above stairs in Ammonite shell display room near end of track. You will needs to drive car through room secured with lasers, then make big jump from ramp that lies at end of room to pick it up. Grabbing Secret Star in Museum 1 will require really fast car, massive rolling start from starting line, and making corner into secured room at very high speed in order to succeed.

SuperMarket 1
thumb|SuperMarket 1 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 11 screenshot
 Name: SuperMarket 1
 Length: 502 meters (479 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Extreme
 Challenge Time: 00:39:000

SuperMarket 1 is eleventh track in the game and first track of Extreme difficulty set in FoodVault market that is much larger than SuperMarket 2 featuring more complex aisles, storage rooms, and cash registers. All racers start at entrance of supermarket beside doors. First section is "Fruits & Vegetables" area with tables that are filled with such food. Right turn is first corner that leads to "Convenience Foods" section with aisles. Unfortunately, that section is blocked by yellow flatbed trolley and cardboard boxes, and racers must instead take sharp left into loading bay that serves as detour. Inside loading bay occurs immediate right turn, then left turn that takes racers onto second floor of bay. Two consecutive right turns then occur here, which must be done while maneuvering around boxes, including mini S-bend around packages. Ramp at end of bay eventually leads racers into aisle section. Four consecutive aisle hairpins occur, all of which are narrow. After fourth turn, path leads into "Freezer Section" where wide left 180 degree turn occurs, leading into small straightaway. At end of straightaway is moderate left corner that leads to sudden sharp right hairpin turn towards three freezer aisles which serve as two lanes. First and third freezer aisles are supported with sacks of potatoes that act as ramp for cars to drive on top of those aisles. At end of aisles is sharp right turn leading into final long straightaway towards row of checkouts where reasonable right turn must be performed after clearing registers. Normal variant of SuperMarket 1 is unlocked when you win Gold Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of SuperMarket 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Extreme tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of SuperMarket 1 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Extreme tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of SuperMarket 1 unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Extreme tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

SuperMarket 1's layout is filled with sharp inclines and consecutive tight corners is nightmare for cars with poor acceleration or turning radius, making them unsuitable to use in this track. Long straightaway near end isn't sufficient enough for cars with high top speeds to use to their advantage. First two slopes in loading bay after start of track are very hard to climb on, especially for cars with poor acceleration. There is floor below top level of loading bay that is used only in Reversed version of SuperMarket 1. Top floor has holes on them in which racers can fall through, thus losing time if they are careless. First tip of the aisle hairpin contain various glass bottles, punishing cars who cross corner too close on inside. There are also cans on outside corners that obstructing racing line. Middle of freezer section is filled with cans stacked as pyramid on top of stands that obstructs racing line through this area. Checkout area is also obstacle because hitting trolleys or registers can make or break race because it's located near start line. Trolleys in particular may be hard to avoid because they are concealed from registers.

Strategies

Cars with excellent acceleration and handling do best in SuperMarket 1 which is track with steep ramps and corners. Many sections of SuperMarket 1 are narrow, so consider using trap Pick Ups like Oil Slick Power-Up, Ball Bearing Power-Up, and Clone Pick Up Power-Up on aisles especially right after sharp corners because opposing racers will have little time to react. Placing Oil Slick Power-Up, Ball Bearing Power-Up, and Clone Pick Up Power-Up in freezer aisles or checkout works too because it will limiting amount of paths that opposing racers can take to get through. There is secret vent opening on "Fruit & Vegetables" section where at end are display shelves located at perimeter of area. Small vent takes racers right to loading zone without making sharp left turn, thus taking them straight to ramp. Another secret route is driving on left of fruit stand that lies right after aisle hairpins. Shortcut forgoes need of making wide 180 degree turn, but is compensated through two sharp 90 degree turns instead. Sadly both options aren't effective when compared to normal route. Hole openings on top floor of loading bay can sometimes be used as advantage. If you gently drop down to lower floor, you can proceed to navigate lower floor and exit quickly. Reduction of air time and ramps here makes this strategy quite valuable. Avoid taking any optional ramps, especially potato bag ramp or register ramps because they will more likely than not cause you to lose precious time.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up can be found in beside straight before cash registers by taking detour to left of left display shelf, making it one of easiest Global Pulse Power-Ups to pick up because it lies along racing line. Nevertheless, taking Global Pulse Power-Up can still be deceiving and risky to grab because it's on straightaway, path where cars can travel at great speed. Going across shelf would mean forgoing lot of speed and time than usual. In Practice mode, Secret Star is on pink-yellow helicopter close to cash register ramps. To collect Secret Star, you must take most leftward ramp and angle you car correctly in order to nab star. Panga is most recommended due to it's good mix of top speed and acceleration, as well as it's large size that makes collecting Secret Star easier than others.

Ghost Town 2
thumb|Ghost Town 2 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 12 screenshot
 Name: Ghost Town 2
 Length: 490 meters (517 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Extreme
 Challenge Time: 00:38:000

Ghost Town 2 is twelfth track in the game and second track of Extreme difficulty set in abandoned Western town where wooden buildings such as general stores, guns shop, banks, hotels, and saloons can be seen throughout entire place just like in Ghost Town 1. Only difference is that racing line is going to different parts of Ghost Town. Second version features entry into abandoned mine which is track's most notable landmark. All racers start at heart of town right after 180 degree turn around gallows as seen in Ghost Town 1. Path to Bargly's Bank is now closed, and this time racers instead take right turn that is now open in this track, leading into small empty shed. Entrance is incline that causes cars to fly right into it. Immediately after exiting house, cars travel towards sidewalk where they will drop off from there and head for path towards abandoned mine that lies just ahead of them. Passageway to abandoned mine consists of soft left turn. After passageway, sharp right must be taken in order to enter mine where there is moderate left turn which gradually decreases in elevation. Incline on bend stops simultaneously as bend finishes, leading into long straightway across tunnel of mine. At end of mine is very small elusive enclosure where racers must bear left to enter it. Soft right occurs inside enclosure that leads into saloon. 90 degree left turn occurs as soon as racers exit saloon that leads to stretch of land used as starting line of Ghost Town 1 where you must head back to starting line through exact same racing line as in Ghost Town 1 which involves heading towards narrow alley that lies besides "Voltstone" building, then driving around perimeter of gallows at central area. As mentioned at beginning of course layout, starting line is right after gallows turn. Normal variant of Ghost Town 2 is unlocked when you win Gold Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of Ghost Town 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Extreme tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Ghost Town 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Extreme tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Ghost Town 2 unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Extreme tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Half of Ghost Town 2's racing line comes from Ghost Town 1, acquiring same hazards in this section. These include existing barrels and crates around gallows, and inconvenient inclines on sidesteps of various buildings. However, addition of mine section makes Ghost Town 2 quite more complex because mine is also littered with barrels and crates. First house which has ramp at entrance is obstacle that will causes you to collide against walls of building if you are careless. Furthermore, there is large pothole after house, causing any car that drives over it to lose speed or flip over, wasting time. Bend inside mine can also be quite tricky because of it's combination of slope and bumpy dirt terrain. Driving too fast around corner may cause cars to spin out of control, especially if their grip is sub-par. Narrow enclosure after mine is also dangerous as well, because it's hotspot for Pick Ups.

Strategies

In Ghost Town 2 that is track with even mix of bends and straights, all-around car is recommended. As with Ghost Town 1, path around gallows is shared, allowing cars who have Electro Pulse Power-Up active to zap any opposing racers that have completed gallows turn, allowing you to catch up. It's recommended that you slow down if you don't feel confident you will win without lots of mistakes, especially with the slope in mine. Losing control there can cost lot of time, making it difficult for you to catch up with opposing racers afterwards. Narrow enclosure right before saloon is xcellent place to deploy trap Pick Ups like Oil Slick Power-Up, Ball Bearing Power-Up, and Clone Pick Up Power-Up because they will guarantee hits from trailing vehicles. Narrow alley just before central area of town is also another decent spot to place Oil Slick Power-Up, Ball Bearing Power-Up, and Clone Pick Up Power-Up.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is in this track one of most deceiving-looking Global Pulse Power-Ups to pick up. Although Global Pulse Power-Up is located right beside mine cart that lies right outside to entrance of mining tunnel, it's obstructed by railings where cars must maneuver around railings to reach cart. In Practice mode, Secret Star is located on top of wall closing fork of balcony and incline used in final section of Ghost Town 1 where you must collide against wall at high speed to grab Secret Star.

Toytanic 2
thumb|Toytanic 2 as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 13 screenshot
 Name: Toytanic 2
 Length: 742 meters (742 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Extreme
 Challenge Time: 00:52:000

Toytanic 2 is thirteenth track in the game and third track of Extreme difficulty set in open seas on ship called Toytanic just like in Toytanic 1. Toytanic 2 and Toytanic 1 use same cruise model and racing line. Difference is weather and start position. Toytanic 1 has sunny weather and race starting on first floor while Toytanic 2 has stormy rainy weather, race starting on top floor, and stronger rocking effect which simulates ocean waves than that in Toytanic 1. All racers start on top floor, where smokestacks and horns of ship are located. Overall, same track rules that are applied for Toytanic 1 are also applied for Toytanic 2, only difference is place of starting line. Normal variant of Toytanic 2 is unlocked when you win Gold Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of Toytanic 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Extreme tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Toytanic 2 is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Extreme tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Toytanic 2 unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Extreme tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Toytanic 2 has stronger rocking effect than Toytanic 1's, as well as slight alteration in trajectory due to rainy weather. As result, changes between top speeds are more erratic which becomes crucial if it occurs before corners because difference between gaining speed before corner and losing speed at straightaway can become quite drastic, requiring factor of luck to win, especially in Time Trial. Toytanic 2 is quite dark, so it may be difficult to see surroundings of track. Fortunately, this may be rectified by increasing brightness under Options. Corner right at entrance of top level becomes more important section of track due to change in starting position. Colliding against wall here, especially in last lap could make or break or race, while in Toytanic 1 making mistake here would be less detrimental because you are given ample time to recover since starting line there is located on lower floors. Aside from these differences, most of obstacles remain same due to the same racing line. These include tight narrow corners especially at second floor of ship where cars may understeer, deck chairs which may obstruct path of various carss, and possibility of falling into pool. Overall, Toytanic 2's difficulty of Extreme remains disputed due to having same course layout as Toytanic 1 that is set at Hard. Toytanic 2 is also considerably easier than Museum 1 as result despite fact that Museum 1 is also listed as Hard.

Strategies

Strategies between Toytanic 1 and Toytanic 2 aren't much different, so there is not need to explain what to do.

Star Locations

Like in Toytanic 1, Global Pulse Power-Up is located on left dead-end corner of steel-meshed enclosure in area right before bottom floor of ship. In Practice mode, Secret Star is located floating in middle of path above front deck of ship, few meters where starting line of Toytanic 1 is. You must use red ramp to collect Secret Star, which by now will be theoertically easier because you will have access to almost every car.

Rooftops
thumb|Rooftops as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 14 screenshot
 Name: Rooftops
 Length: 588 meters (588 meters in Reverse)
 Difficulty: Medium
 Challenge Time: 00:54:000

Rooftops is fourteenth track in the game and fourth track of Medium Difficulty set in urban city at night where cars jump from building to building in order to complete laps. All racers start on top of building with three arches where another building lies right in front of them, which they must jump across as soon as race starts. A sharp right occurs in this building, where vehicles then drive over the window panels located on roof. After navigating through panels, racers jump across building with capsule-shaped canopy, and go around perimeter of this building by making two consecutive 90 degree right turns. At end of second building is jump to next building that has helicopter pad on top of it's roof with actual helicopter hovering above it. On landing pad, cars must make quick left turn which takes them out of spot onto next building. Another left turn occurs, which is yet another jump. On building consisting of two satellite dishes is soft right turn leading into inclined walkway that takes racers onto main control room of dishes where they must go around building by making two back-to-back right turns. After making these turns, another inclined walkway is seen, taking racers to next building that is fairly long straightaway with bumps across route. Racers are then taken to building with three horizontal pillars, where after passing them is sharp 90 degree right turn. Very sharp incline is seen ahead where it's necessary to climb it. After incline, there is straightaway where first building with arches is not too far away.  Normal variant of Rooftops is unlocked when you win Bronze Cup in Championship mode. Mirrored variant of Rooftops is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all Medium tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse variant of Rooftops is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all reversed versions of Medium tracks in Time Trial mode. Reverse-Mirrored variant of Rooftops is unlocked when you beat Challenge times for all mirrored versions of Medium tracks in Time Trial mode.

Obstacles

Many obstacles on Rooftops are formed by ramps and elevations on roofs like ceiling windows for instance. Multiple scenarios of these ramps is negative impact for cars with poor acceleration and stability because it will cause them to feel slow and sluggish as they cross inclines, as well as make them lose control after jumps. You could fall off building's rooftops to their doom if they are careless, forcing automatic reposition. Cans of paint, stairs, and spotlights at heliport are obstacles all around track.

Strategies

Due to countless amount of bumps and jumps, car with good acceleration or stability is recommended. For maximum impact, it's good idea to place Pick Ups like Oil Slick Power-Up and Clone Pick Up Power-Up on peak of buildings's ramps. That way, any opposing cars that come across them will lose control onto next building, hindering their landing. Furthermore, attempt to cut corners when navigating from one building to another, especially helicopter pad, as this will save you time in long run. At very sharp incline near end, head across incline to side rather than ahead because it's less steep from that section.

Star Locations

Global Pulse Power-Up is located in alley enclosure just behind second steel ramp where it's easier to grabit in Reverse version of Rooftoops because it's readily visible in that direction. In Practice mode, Secret Star is located at end of the top of wall surrounding satellite headquarters which is seriously hard to reach. You must head towards second steel ramp at opposite direction instead of entering ramp on right side of steel ramp. Then, cross edge of building at moderate to slow speed to land on top of wall. As soon as landing occurs, you must come to complete stop in order to prevent accidental falling off wall after landing, which will all take few attempts and degree of luck to succeed. There, drive carefully around perimeter of wall where Secret Star is located at end.

Stunt Arena
thumb|Stunt Arena as seen in track selection
thumb|Track 15 screenshot
 Name: Stunt Arena
 Track: Neighbourhood Arena

Stunt Arena is fifteen track in the game where you must collect all 20 Secret Stars scattered across entire track. Stunt Arena is good track to do stunts varying from loops to jumps. Secret Stars flying above top of archway leading into half pipe are hardest because of how high they are, and only car that can grab them successfully is Probe UFO. While arch is flanked by steep hills which make getting to top very hard, left side (facing entrance from outside) of arch has
small, even patch of land next to top that make getting up there bit easier. Enter half pipe and make sure to face front of car so that it will be heading toward that flat grassing area after leaping into air and veer bit left as car takes it's final path up half pipe before leaping. Just before and while it your car is airborne, hold left and hope it lands safely while being quick to come to complete stop. Then drive toward stars to collect them. Besides those above top of archway, Secret Stars in looped ramp are also hard to collect, especially one in center because you must drop at right time and at right height, for which again you will need Probe UFO. Afterwards, collecting rest of Secret Stars should be fairly easy. Overall, Probe UFO is key car to collect all Secret Stars in Stunt Arena. Once you collect all Secret Stars in Stunt Arena, you will unlock Clockwork Carnage mode where only clockwork cars are present.
